MappedPercent.note: Bismark's percent of reads with a unique best alignment (MultiQC 1.32 bismark module, general-stats column percent_aligned). The alternate, samtools stats on the bwa-meth and bwa-mem alignments as in the rnaseq map, counts any mapped read, multimapped included, so the two paths' values do not mean the same thing; key unverified until a real run

DuplicationPercent.note: Bismark deduplicate's percent of alignments removed as duplicates (MultiQC 1.32 bismark module, general-stats column dup_reads_percent); the alternate is Picard MarkDuplicates on the bwa-meth and bwa-mem paths, as in the rnaseq map; key unverified until a real run

deliberately_unmapped.why: Number of cytosines analysed, in millions (MultiQC divides by a million): a count, and D.SEQ has no field for it.
Count of uniquely aligned reads, scaled by MultiQC's read-count multiplier (millions by default); MappedPercent records the aligned share from the same Bismark report.
Count of alignments left after deduplication, scaled by MultiQC's read-count multiplier (millions by default); DuplicationPercent records the duplicate share from the same report.
Percentage of bases (not reads) trimmed by Trim Galore; low signal, as ruled for riboseq.

methylseq runs FastQC twice (raw reads, then Trim Galore's trimmed reads) under one MultiQC fastqc section, and a single-end sample's two reports get the same row name, so MultiQC keeps one and overwrites the other: which reads the value describes is unknown. Bisulfite conversion also leaves read GC near 20 percent whatever the library.

methylseq's raw and trimmed FastQC reports share one row name for a single-end sample and MultiQC overwrites one with the other, so this may be the length after trimming, not the sequenced read length F_bp means.
Same as the average length; hidden when samples agree within 10 bp.
Sequence-level duplication before alignment; DuplicationPercent is alignment-based (Bismark deduplicate or Picard), and mixing the two definitions in one field would mislead.
Share of FastQC modules that failed: a report summary, not a measurement.
Count in millions; NumReads/TotalReads hold read counts.

On the bwa-meth and bwa-mem paths, samtools counts every bisulfite C-to-T (or TAPS) conversion as a mismatch against the reference, so the rate measures conversion as much as sequencing error; MismatchPercent would mislead.
BAM-record count in millions, both mates of a pair counted: no stand-in for TotalReads.
BAM-record count in millions; MappedPercent records the mapped share.
Secondary and supplementary BAM records, in millions: a record count, not a share, and D.SEQ has no attribute for it.
Sits near 100 on paired-end bwa alignments and is absent for single-end data, so it tells samples apart by nothing.
Reads with mapping quality 0: as much a property of the reference's repeats as of the library, and not the multimapped share MultimappedPercent holds.
Mean insert size of the aligned pairs. D.SEQ has no insert-size attribute; one would be a schema request, not a mapping.

unmapped_files.why: Bismark's alignment reports (bismark and bismark_hisat); their numbers are read through MultiQC.
samtools stats, flagstat and idxstats on the bwa-meth and bwa-mem alignments; their numbers are read through MultiQC.
Unmapped reads as FASTQ (with --unmapped): leftovers of the alignment, not a result.
Bismark's unsorted alignment (with --save_align_intermeds, --skip_deduplication or --rrbs): the same reads as the sorted BAM the aln rule registers, before sorting.
Bismark deduplication reports; the duplicate share is read through MultiQC.
Picard MarkDuplicates metrics on the bwa-meth and bwa-mem paths; the duplicate share is read through MultiQC.
Bismark's per-read, per-context cytosine calls (CpG, CHG, CHH by strand): large, and every CpG value in them is summarised in the coverage file the mseq_bismark rule registers.
The bedGraph limited to the target BED (with --run_targeted_sequencing): a subset of the registered row's bedGraph companion, and A.MSEQ has no Notes to carry a second companion.
Bismark coverage2cytosine reports and coverage (with --cytosine_report or --nomeseq): no rule yet (see "Outputs with no rule yet" in the README).

MethylDackel's non-CpG calls (with --all_contexts), as bedGraph or, with --methyl_kit, methylKit: no rule yet, and A.MSEQ has one secondary-file slot and no Notes (see "Outputs with no rule yet" in the README).
MethylDackel's calls limited to the target BED (with --run_targeted_sequencing): a subset of the registered CpG bedGraph.
Rastair's TAPS methylation calls on the bwa-mem path: no rule yet (see "Outputs with no rule yet" in the README).
Bismark's M-bias tables and methylation-extractor reports: QC read through MultiQC.
MethylDackel's M-bias tables: QC of the extraction, not a result.
Rastair's conversion-by-position tables and the trimming they set for its caller: QC and an intermediate, not a result.
Bismark's per-sample HTML reports; their numbers are read through MultiQC.
Bismark's run summary report; its numbers are read through MultiQC.
Qualimap BamQC reports (with --run_qualimap); their numbers are read through MultiQC.
Preseq library-complexity curves (with --run_preseq): plotted in MultiQC, not a sample result.
Picard CollectHsMetrics on target-capture runs (with --run_targeted_sequencing and --collecthsmetrics); read through MultiQC.
Aligner indexes built from the reference (with --save_reference): reference files, not sample data.
FastQC reports on the raw reads; their numbers are read through MultiQC.
Trim Galore logs, FastQC of the trimmed reads, and the trimmed reads themselves (with --save_trimmed): an intermediate of the registered alignment.
Lanes of one sample concatenated into one FASTQ: an input to the alignment, not a result.
